Part 2&3 地点 PLACE

Describe a city you enjoyed visiting

描述一个你游览得很开心的城市

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a city you enjoyed visiting

  • Where it is (它在哪里)
  • When you visited it (你什么时候去的)
  • How long you stayed there (你在那里待了多久)
  • What you did there (你在那里做了什么)
  • And explain why you enjoyed visiting it (并解释为什么你喜欢游览这座城市)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a city you enjoyed visiting

I'd like to talk about Nanning, which is the capital city of Guangxi province in the south of China. I went there with my girlfriend about a year ago, during a long holiday, and we stayed for roughly four days. Actually, the trip was her idea. She had visited Nanning before and kept saying how relaxed the city felt, so we decided to spend the break there instead of staying in Shenzhen, where we both live. While we were there, we did quite a lot. On the first day, we climbed Qingxiu Mountain, which was a bit tiring, but the view from the top over the whole city made it worthwhile. We also walked around Guangxi University, and I remember it felt much quieter and greener than the campuses back home. In the evenings, we went to the night market and tried lots of local dishes, like laoyou noodles, which is a famous rice noodle dish from Nanning. To be honest, I ate way too much, but I have no regrets. The reason I enjoyed it so much is that the whole trip was genuinely relaxing. The city has a slower pace of life than Shenzhen, with trees and parks everywhere, and my girlfriend was really happy, which made me happy too. Looking back, it wasn't a fancy trip, just good food, good company and a change of scenery. So that's why Nanning is a city I really enjoyed visiting.

南宁是广西首府，位于中国南部；一年前和女朋友去旅游，待了大约四天。是女朋友提议的，她去过南宁说很放松。活动：爬青秀山看全城景色、逛广西大学、晚上去夜市吃老友粉等本地美食。喜欢的原因：节奏比深圳慢、绿化多、女朋友开心、美食好吃，换个环境很放松。

Q2What kinds of facilities do big cities have?

Big cities usually offer a wide range of facilities. To start with, there's the transport system, including the metro, buses and high-speed rail, which make getting around convenient. Then there are shopping malls, hospitals, schools and universities, which cover people's daily needs. Most cities also have cultural facilities, such as museums, libraries and parks, which improve quality of life. I think it's this combination that makes a city feel comfortable to live in.

大城市设施齐全：交通（地铁/公交/高铁）、商场、医院、学校，还有博物馆、图书馆、公园等文化设施；正是这些组合让城市生活方便舒适。

Q3Do you think modern cities are suitable for young people or old people?

I'd say modern cities suit young people more, at least in most cases. Young people benefit from the job opportunities and the overall convenience. Older people, on the other hand, often prefer quieter surroundings and stronger community ties, which cities tend to lack. That said, it depends on the individual. Some elderly people appreciate easy access to hospitals and shops. So on balance, modern cities work better for the young, though they can suit older people too.

现代城市更适合年轻人：就业机会多、生活便利；老人更偏好安静和社区感，但看个人，有的老人也享受就医购物的便利。总体偏年轻人。

Q4Before you travel to a city, what factors would you consider?

For me, a few things matter. First, the budget, because accommodation and transport can be expensive, so I usually set a rough limit before I go. Then the weather, since I don't enjoy sightseeing in extreme heat or heavy rain. And perhaps most importantly, what the city has to offer, like food, culture or natural scenery, because I want the trip to feel worthwhile. When I planned my trip to Nanning, the local food was the biggest draw for me.

出行前考虑三点：预算（吃住行可能贵）、天气（不喜欢酷热暴雨）、城市特色（美食/文化/自然风光）；去南宁就是被美食吸引的。

Q5What are the disadvantages of living in a very famous city?

There are quite a few, actually. The most obvious one is the cost of living, since famous cities usually have expensive housing and high daily expenses, which puts pressure on ordinary people. Another downside is overcrowding, especially at tourist attractions, which makes them hard to enjoy during peak seasons. I also think there's a subtler problem: famous cities can become over-commercialised and lose their local character. So while they're exciting to visit, living there day to day can be exhausting.

著名城市缺点：生活成本高（房价贵）、拥挤（旅游旺季难享受）、过度商业化导致本地特色流失；适合旅游但长期居住很累。

Q6Do you prefer to visit well-developed cities or cities with a long history?

I'd probably choose cities with a long history, though it depends on the mood I'm in. Developed cities can feel a bit similar, with the same malls and skyscrapers, whereas historic cities offer something unique, like old streets, traditional food and their stories. Having said that, developed cities are more comfortable to travel in, with better transport and hotels. So I lean towards historic cities for the experience, though I appreciate the convenience of modern ones too.

更倾向历史名城：有古街、传统美食和故事；发达城市虽方便但千篇一律。视心情而定，两者都欣赏。

Q7For those who live in cities, is it because they want to or have to?

I think it's a mix, but for many people it's more of a necessity. The main reason is work, because most job opportunities are concentrated in cities, which means people have to move there to make a living. Having said that, once they've settled in, many of them come to enjoy it, thanks to the convenience and the lifestyle. So I'd say people mostly move to cities because they have to, but many end up staying because they want to.

多数人搬进城市是不得不（工作机会集中在城市），但定居后很多人真正喜欢上城市生活；先因为需要，后因为想要。
